questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I chose an English-speaking country, as I didn't want language to be a barrier when speaking with locals or an obstacle when choosing my courses. Also, I chose a university which seemed used to handling visiting students which made the whole experience much simpler as information was easy to come by and help was only an email
away.The
housing was a great deal more expensive than anticipated, but living with other students was a great way to meet new people.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. We had orientation and a third party had made a WhatsApp group, so you could ask questions there as well

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had orientation, but a lot was just learning as you go by speaking with other visiting students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I thought I would get housing through the university but that took too long, so I googled and then booked myself. It was easy to find, but expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Pick something either close to the city (what I did) or to the university. Living far away from both just means you spend a lot of time in transportation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We received different emails before arriving describing everything we needed to do and how (including screenshots) and which days the different things had to be done.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Just email the international office and they would answer quickly. Or after arriving we could always just show up and ask for help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I picked my courses from home, but after arriving changed one of them. Afterwards, I wished I had changed one other course but other than that I was really happy about the courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Read the emails carefully -all the information is there.
Also, when picking your courses check the grading. I had continuous assessment in all my courses and an end of term exam. I wished I had picked some with only continuous assessment, as I then wouldn't have ended up with so much work at the end of my exchange.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I needed some introductory courses, and level was therefore as according. 
The other courses was easy to follow along with but I still learned something

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Very different. I had 6 courses of 5 ECTS each. In most (5 out of 6) I had 2 one-hour lectures and one lab spread out over the week. This meant that I had several "holes" in my time table which I used to study or chat with friends.
Also, the only reading material I had was lecture slides

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CS1069: Introduction to Internet Technologies
CS1106: Introduction to Relational Databases
CS1111: Systems Organisation
CS2513: Intermediate Programming
ST2053: Introduction to Regression Analysis
CC1110: The Ancient Celts: Origins

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ST2053: Introduction to Regression Analysis and really well structured

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Housing was more expensive than expected, and I had to buy practical stuff such as duvets etc.
Also, I paid 2.5 euro per wash or drying

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and public transportation was less than I was used to

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So much. They had clubs and societies for pretty much anything. I huge sport center was also available for all students for free (so no need to pay for a fitness subscription).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Climbing was really fun (and free).
Go on as many trips as possible: you are only there for a short time so enjoy.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you are up for it rent a car (in Ireland you drive in the left side, and if you are younger than 25 it is a bit more expensive), fill it up with friends and drive to Mizen Head, drive the ring of Kerry, see Dingle Peninsula . From Cork you can also take public transportation to Cork, Kinsale (Old head is really beautiful), rock of Cashel and much more. It is also worth a trip to Dublin and Galway (while in Galway/on the way there, see the cliffs of Mohr).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are very friendly. Just talk to them, but in my experience, you tend to spend most of your time with other international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Going out for a pint is totally normal any day of  the week. People are really friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Cork International Students organize a lot of stuff for international students so join their Facebook/WhatsApp group.
Join clubs and societies that interest you and meet new people.
Pick courses you like, and change them quickly if you are not sure

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting some truly amazing people and experience the Irish culture with them

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Going there all on my own without knowing anyone or anything about the town or the people.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
